title: CNF-SAT by number of variables
task: Does the formula have a satisfying assignment?
encoding: An explicitly listed Boolean CNF formula with no fixed bound on clause width.
parameter: The number of occurring variables n.
coverage: Historical ETH and effective bounds under FPT ≠ W[1].

reader.parameter: The number of occurring variables n.

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm decides CNF-SAT within the stated running time.

sources.role: historical 3SAT hypothesis by number of variables

sourceBasis.step: A CNF-SAT algorithm with the stated running time applies in particular to width-three formulas with the same variable count.

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides CNF-SAT within the stated running time.

sourceBasis.step: For each paired variable pair in the Cai–Juedes construction, two CNF clauses enforce exactly one true variable without adding variables. The CNF has O(h log r) variables for source weight h and r source variables. A computable exponent cutoff then bounds CNF-SAT time by a fixed power of r times a computable function of h, which would decide the W[1]-hard source problem in FPT time.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: Both exclusions use the number of occurring variables. The recovery requires a computable convergence cutoff and uses the same polynomial factor in the complete input length.
